#5044. Tether-backed Twenty One Capital reports $1.09 billion Q3 net income on bitcoin gains

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

CEO Rapha Zagury said fair-value crypto gains are a starting point as the firm evaluates mining, lending and potential share buybacks.

Twenty One Capital Twenty One Capital (XXI) reported third-quarter net income of $1.087 billion, almost entirely from $1.093 billion in fair value gains on its bitcoin holdings, according to an SEC filing.

The Tether-backed company held 43,514 BTC as of Sept. 30, valued at roughly $83,700 per BTC, plus $102.8 million in cash and cash equivalents. Its convertible notes carried $486.5 million in principal and were collateralized by about 16,116 BTC.

Twenty One Capital also recorded a $4.8 million operating loss and $1.34 million in interest expense for the three months ended Sept. 30, the filing shows.  For the first nine months of 2026, it reported a net loss of $186.5 million, reflecting bitcoin's price decline.

CEO Rapha Zagury acknowledged the results but said, "A balance sheet is not a business. It is our starting point."

"We welcome Bitcoin’s appreciation," Zagury wrote in a letter to shareholders. "But gains from an asset we own are not the same as earnings from businesses we operate. Building the latter is our job."

Zagury said the company was evaluating opportunities across bitcoin mining, lending, treasury and energy. The company would consider buying back shares when they trade below the value of the assets attributable to them, according to the CEO.

Twenty One Capital was established with backing from Tether, Bitfinex and SoftBank in April last year, with the USDT issuer subsequently acquiring SoftBank's stake this May.

The company's shares fell 19.48% over the past month, compared with Bitcoin's 16.06% decline over the same period, according to The Block's data.

#5042. Illinois Crypto Tax Draws Unlikely Alliance of DOJ, Banks and DeFi

Illinois Crypto Tax Draws Unlikely Alliance of DOJ, Banks and DeFi

An unusually broad coalition, spanning the U.S. Justice Department, Wall Street’s biggest lobby, the national Chamber of Commerce and a who’s-who of crypto firms, has thrown its weight behind a legal challenge to Illinois’ first-of-its-kind tax on digital asset transactions.

The groups filed briefs this month in Illinois state court supporting a lawsuit from the Crypto Council for Innovation and the Blockchain Association, which are asking a judge to strike down the state’s Digital Asset Tax Act and permanently block its enforcement.

The tax imposes a 0.2% levy on the full value of a digital asset every time an Illinois customer trades, transfers, or stores it through a broker, even when there’s no sale, gain, or change in ownership.

Critics have called it among the most punitive crypto taxes in the country, in part because Illinois imposes no comparable tax on dollars, gold, stocks or any other asset, and no other state has anything like it.

On Nov. 6, the Justice Department filed a statement of interest arguing the tax undermines federal policy and U.S. leadership in digital assets, calling it vague and discriminatory for singling out crypto for treatment no other asset faces.

The U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association, which represents hundreds of broker-dealers, banks and asset managers, filed an amicus brief warning the tax reaches well beyond crypto-native platforms to the traditional banks, custodians and advisers increasingly offering digital asset products.

A separate brief filed Nov. 11 brought together crypto’s heavy hitters, led by the DeFi Education Fund, Andreessen Horowitz, Paradigm and Uniswap, and including Aave Labs, Chainlink Labs, Solana Policy Institute, Phantom, Jito Labs, Multicoin Capital and Stand With Crypto.

Their filing argues the law’s definitions are so vague they could stretch to software developers and decentralized protocols that hold no customer funds and have no way to identify users or know where a transaction occurred. The brief noted an estimated 2.64 million Illinoisans hold digital assets, the fifth-highest total of any state.

“This tax is unclear, discriminatory, unconstitutional, and harmful to the future of finance,” CCI CEO Ji Hun Kim and Blockchain Association executive Ashok Pinto said in a joint statement.

The challenge dates to August. As Decrypt reported, Illinois agreed in October to pause the tax until July 1, 2027, buying time for the court fight now underway.

#5041. This Guy Lost 54 Pounds and Got Absolutely Shredded in 6 Months

At 46, Austin Cowburn wanted to overcome injuries and get back to feeling his best. Here’s how he did it.

At age 46, Austin Cowburn felt his training was "directionless," and he started putting on weight. This former runner and marathoner wanted to overcome injuries and get back to feeling his best. Here’s how he did it.

RUNNING HAS ALWAYS been my go-to exercise; as a younger man I joined several running clubs, and even finished as even finished pretty high up in the 1995 New York Marathon. I spent weeknights and Saturday mornings on the track or in a swimming pool. Cardio is familiar to me, and as I grew up, I stuck with it. Looking back, I realize means I didn’t have the understanding and technique to really benefit from weight training.

After a couple of years of directionless training, plus two injuries and rehab, and a poor diet, I put on weight. That inflamed other, niggling injuries, which made me feel like I just wasn’t at my best. I felt sluggish; my favorite clothes didn’t fit as well, and the new ones seemed to be smaller than I expected. I wanted to get back into marathons, but to do that I need to get fitter, stronger, and healthier. So, I approached Ultimate Performance Manchester for help.

We started with fundamental stuff: monitoring and being consistent with my diet. I went from eating a lot of rich, calorie-laden food, eating it at all times of the day, to something much more sustainable. I’d enjoy a blended berry smoothie in the morning with protein, and three scrambled eggs with spinach in mid-morning. Mid-afternoon and evening, I’d eat lean-meat chili, mainly turkey mince, with lots of vegetables thrown in, including peppers and tomatoes, as well as rice. I also enjoyed a low-fat, high-protein yogurt in the evening mixed with banana, honey, or chia seeds. On the weekend, I could indulge in a nice steak.

We often forget how big an impact diet can have on mood, energy levels, and your ability to train hard and get the best from yourself. Changing what I ate really reminded me of the importance of a foundational diet.

I trained three times a week in the gym, usually from 8 a.m. to 9 a.m. I loved getting it done first thing in the morning, which really set me up for the day. I would also run four times a week. I really got my love for running back during this time: my distances increased, and I had no injuries. I didn’t even have aches and pains afterward. Training, losing weight, and fueling my body correctly really helped me regain my fluidity of motion.

It also helped with my energy levels and sleep. I felt mentally sharper, more productive and more creative. People told me that my skin was glowing. Everyone was extremely positive and kind in and out of the gym, complimentary, and really encouraging. My family was very proud and surprised with the results, and I felt like the very best version of myself.

In six months, I lost 24.6 kg (54 pounds), bringing my body fat percentage from 28.2% to 11.6%. I dropped from an extra-large to a medium. I’ve continued training, and now I’m eating more, and building muscle mass. I’m looking to sustain my gains and also increase the number of exercises I have in my toolbox.

It’s great to be able to say that more, better training has helped me avoid injuries. The more I trained, the more I wanted to, and my stamina has gone through the roof. I’m happier, more relaxed, and more motivated; I just feel better about myself.

I think anyone can do this, and if you’re on the fence about it, just go for it. Set clear goals and look for help, whether that’s a professional trainer or just a friend who’ll hold you accountable. You don’t have to change all at once; I’d recommend not putting too much pressure on yourself from session to session. Enjoy your exercises; make sure you rest and refuel correctly.

#5040. The 7 Best Microcurrent Devices of 2026 Tested by Women’s Health Editors

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

We’re living in the golden age of high-tech skincare devices—and as our beauty editor, I couldn’t be happier. Red light therapy devices, including LED face masks, provide excellent anti-aging benefits from the comfort of our couch, while face steamers have replaced my need for pricey spa facials. Laser hair removal devices are becoming more inclusive by offering technology safe enough for deeper complexions. Face massagers also help de-puff skin after a hangover. However, when it comes to lifting saggy skin, microcurrent devices are the ultimate MVP skincare tool deserving of a spot in your beauty arsenal.

Think of them as a sculpting workout for your face without the sweat. “Microcurrent devices use low levels of electrical current to stimulate facial muscles, helping to boost collagen and sculpt and lift the face,” says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD. And don’t worry: These aren’t painful. You’ll notice more of a temporary tingling sensation that’ll disappear within minutes of using the device.

While these at-home machines aren’t as powerful as the ones used by professionals, they’re a more cost-effective option for achieving subtle improvements, says dermatologist Bradley Glodny, MD. You’ll just need some patience to find a weekly cadence and intensity level that works for you. (More on that in a bit.) And if you’re getting seasonal in-office microcurrent treatments, these at-home machines help enhance and sustain your professional results over time, says Dr. Garshick.

What was once a closely guarded secret among my fellow beauty editors and plastic surgeons has now become increasingly popular and readily accessible across our most trusted sites, such as Sephora, Ulta, and Amazon. But an influx of hundreds of options can be overwhelming, which is where I come in. My years of reporting and research have informed this shopping guide. I also consulted the pros about what to look out for when buying at-home microcurrent machines. Ahead are a few non-negotiables to keep in mind, which helped inform the devices we tested and ultimately featured in this story.

Most devices on this list have a range of microcurrent levels—some, like Foreo, even go up to 10. The higher you go, the more intense the microcurrent will feel. If you're accustomed to microcurrent and prefer a device with more power and customization options, opt for one that offers multiple microcurrent levels.

On the other hand, if you're a beginner, you might only need to purchase a device with a few microcurrent levels, such as the NuFace Trinity.

Dr. Garshick advises using your microcurrent device at least three times a week for four to six weeks before you can expect to see results, although some devices recommend daily use. “While much of the initial benefit may only be noticed for hours to days, with consistent use, the results will continue as collagen production can take six or more months,” she says.

After the initial treatment period, you can decrease the frequency of treatments to two to three times per week to maintain your results. Always refer to the specific instructions for use of your microcurrent device.

Many microcurrent devices come with additional features, such as interchangeable attachments, smartphone app connectivity, and even instructional guides.

An added bonus for your microcurrent device is FDA approval, which means that the government organization has determined that the device is safe and effective for its intended use. This is not a necessity when purchasing a microcurrent device, but it's definitely a solid addition if you're looking for something that has been rigorously tested.

You’ll also want to order a microcurrent device that either includes a priming gel or purchase one separately. They’re conductive and allow the electrical currents to be transmitted from the device to the skin. They also help the device glide easily across the skin and help prevent irritation.

Unlike bulky in-office machines, at-home microcurrent devices are about the size of a closed fist. #5038. Kraken parent Payward posts 66% drop in Q3 adjusted EBITDA, plans US prediction markets and personal finance AI agent

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

Transaction volume rose 22% from the second quarter to $353 billion, down 30% from a year earlier.

Kraken parent Payward reported $60 million in third-quarter adjusted EBITDA on Friday, up from $23 million in the second quarter, but down by about two-thirds from the $178.6 million it posted a year earlier.

Payward replaced adjusted revenue with a measure it calls "total platform margin," which also deducts staking rewards paid to customers. Total platform margin rose to $487 million in Q3 from $436 million in Q2, according to the private company's financial highlights released Friday, but fell 12% year over year.

Customers transacted $353 billion across Payward's platforms during the quarter, with volume down 30% from a year earlier but up 22% from the second quarter.

Payward said it ended September with 7.1 million funded accounts, up 7% from Q2 and 37% year over year. Billable accounts stood at 1.5 million, up 9% from Q2 and 74% year over year.

Payward said prediction markets for U.S. clients are among the new products next on its roadmap. Payward Chief Commercial Officer Mark Greenberg had discussed a possible rollout on CNBC last December, though Friday's update gave no planned launch date.

Payward also plans to offer stock perpetual futures through its own CFTC-regulated exchange, clearinghouse, and broker, build apps for local markets, and let customers share collateral across products in one account. It also plans to settle U.S. dollar wires through its Federal Reserve master account, test a U.S. credit card, and fund lending in Europe with customer deposits.

On Wednesday, Payward added more than 200 tokenized UK and European equities to xStocks. In Friday's update, it said it is developing funds built around xStocks, which surpassed $1 billion in AUM in October, and plans to launch xPO, which would let private companies raise capital by issuing shares onchain, subject to regulatory approval.

LISTEN, NO ONE is going to say you must trim your pubic hair, but a little over half of all men do. Shaving, trimming, or hell, even getting a manzillian, comes down to a personal decision in both the how and why. Some guys like the way it feels, some like the way it looks, and some get a confidence boost knowing that they’re well-groomed down there. Whatever your reasons for below-the-belt manscaping, the most important thing to consider before you start is what tools you’re going to use to do it.

Trimmers are a great option for body grooming because they offer a variety of options. Most of them, at least the ones designed for the delicate groin area, have features to help protect the skin on your penis, scrotum, and surrounding areas from nicks and cuts.

They also usually have length attachments so you can choose exactly how long you want your hair (and even change it up as desired). Still, if you favor a close, hairless shave, you may want to turn to your old standbys: a razor and shaving cream. Whichever tool you ultimately choose will come down to a few factors based on your unique preferences. These are the seven best options across the board.

When it comes to pubic hair trimming, it’s all about balancing risk versus results. When you’re trimming or shaving delicate skin below the belt, you need to be careful, and this trimmer helps minimize risk. Specifically designed for your groin area, the blades are more closely spaced to help prevent snags, and the attachments help protect your skin from direct contact with the razor.

Testing Notes: This trimmer makes the case for using tools specifically designed for the area you’re grooming. I found in my testing that its blades are more closely placed than your traditional trimmer to help prevent skin from being caught between them. They actually make a difference when trimming your delicate nether regions.

All the features packed into this trimmer make the experience of trimming your groin as easy as possible and minimize cut risk, while the skin-protecting attachment does a great job of providing further distance between your skin and the blade. The one thing to note about this trimmer, however, is that if you prefer a clean shave, this will not deliver it by itself.

While it will trim very close, even with the attachment, it’s not going to give you a smooth, clean finish. You may want to use this trimmer to trim down the carpet first before moving in with a traditional razor. Also, if you’re hoping to trim other parts of your body, like your head or face (which I wouldn’t recommend for sanitary reasons), you may not find this trimmer powerful enough for the thicker hair that’s found in those locations.

Honestly, is there something the Philips OneBlade can’t do? Since its launch, this trimmer and shaver has become an iconic grooming essential, and for good reason. It’s incredibly easy to use, hardly ever nicks or cuts skin, and can shave and trim with equally good results. This version even comes with more length attachments that allow you to get your ideal manscaping results with ease.

Testing Notes: In all of my trimmer and shaver testing, no matter what kind, the Philips OneBlade stands out among the pack because it’s just so darn easy to use. Unlike your typical trimmers, the innovative head is shaped like a razor and can cut hair in both directions, making it foolproof.

There is also something about the razor, even when used without any attachments, that hardly ever cuts skin, even when you’re using it on your delicate areas below the belt. Since it’s designed for body grooming, the OneBlade features more attachments than the original, but you still won’t be able to leave hair super long.

The plus side of getting quite as close as other trimming options means it’s nearly impossible to cut yourself—even if you’re using it without a guard. Whenever someone is nervous about nicking their nuts, this is my top recommendation.

It’s best for people who like a close trim or a shave. The small size and light weight make it easy to take with you wherever you go, and I had no issue with the battery life, even though it’s not quite as long as some others on this list.

I also appreciate that it comes with a second blade, so you can easily switch them when you use this on your face (you don’t want to use the same blade on your face and body because of the possibility of cross-contamination).

This trimmer is chock-full of cool features that are the sort of thing you didn’t know you needed until you have them, like a built-in LED light for seamless groinal navigation, a travel lock to avoid slicing through clothes or other products in your Dopp kit, and a nifty low-battery light to let you know it’s time to recharge before diving into a trim.

This trimmer is built for below-the-belt grooming but works great on other body parts too. It trims quickly and efficiently, no matter where you use it. The 5.0 is also fully waterproof and armed with a protective outer guard above the blades to minimize the risk of nicks or cuts.

Testing Notes: In my testing, I found a lot to love about the newest version of the Lawn Mower. Compared to previous models, it seems to cut a little bit easier and more efficiently, and with less snagging. The blade guard really does help in this department, though I did experience a few nicks when trying to trim too quickly (never a good idea when dealing with the groin, to be honest).

I don’t recommend using it without the guard, as the blades can be a little harsh on bare skin. However, a natural side effect of this is that you won’t ever get a completely bald shave with this device. Still, it’s surprisingly lightweight, and the added features like the built-in light make the experience of groin trimming as pleasant as it can be. It also corrected one of the more annoying issues with previous models by adding a travel lock on its power button that requires more effort to activate.

Unlike previous models, the 5.0 does not include a charging dock; however, it is fully equipped with USB-C charging capabilities, which I much prefer to the dock. I’d argue that every electric device should be required to use this much more universal charger. It saves on space by limiting the amount of wires you need laying around, and is far more convenient to replace if you ever lose the included cord.

Meridian’s body trimmer helps prevent irritation, tugging, and nicks with its high-precision ceramic blades. Slicing your skin when manscaping, especially if you’re new to it, can produce serious panic, which is why Meridian went with ceramic blades. In comparison to steel or plastic, ceramic blades stay sharper longer, generate less heat, and glide smoothly across sensitive skin.

This makes Meridian’s trimmer ideal for beginners or anyone nervous about trimming sensitive areas. Plus, it’s waterproof and easy to use. There aren’t any complicated settings or tech involved, and just two guards to choose from. For beginners, this is perfect. It limits any learning curve beyond getting over the initial hump of anxiety for where you’re taking a blade.

Testing Notes: Meridian highlights two key benefits of its pubic trimmer: safety and speed—even claiming you can finish a full job in under 60 seconds. While I can confirm it’s powerful enough to mow through hair fast, no one should approach grooming with that expectation. Rushing, especially on sensitive areas, is a quick way to end up with nicks and cuts.

In terms of safety, I found this trimmer rarely—if ever—caused cuts or irritation. However, that safety seems to come at the cost of precision. I often had to go over the same spot multiple times to get a close shave. While the ceramic blades boost protection, they just don’t shave as closely as stainless steel.

Braun built this trimmer to power through all kinds of hair, no matter the length or location. With adjustable settings offering up to 40 lengths, it trims nose hairs just as easily as it delivers a crew cut. Its powerful motor and precision make it a top choice for anyone with thick body hair or an untamed look down below, where other trimmers often fall short.

Testing Notes: I love the wide-ranging length options the Braun All-In-One Series 9 offers that allow for true head-to-toe grooming. The adjustable length dial particularly makes transitioning from one part of your body to another seamless and quick for those in a hurry. Now, I wouldn’t recommend using the same trimmer for your face and body, but this device certainly has the agility and horsepower to handle all areas smoothly.

I also dig how sleek the charging dock is and, crucially, how little space it takes up on the bathroom counter. That being said, while Braun boasts about the Series 9’s 180-minute charging runtime, my testing found it’s in the 120-minute range. Still an impressive burst from one charge, but not quite 180 minutes.

Read More: Braun Series 9 Style Kit Review

Using a disposable razor for pubic shaving is great because it minimizes the risk of cross-contamination, and you ensure that your blades are always sharp and ready to cut. This disposable razor has five gentle blades that, while not specifically designed for the groin, are designed for the most sensitive skin, making it perfect for the area.

Testing Notes: Conventional wisdom says that using fewer blades is ideal for shaving the pubic area, as razors with multiple blades often increase the risk of irritation, razor bumps, and ingrown hairs. These issues tend to arise when the blades cut hair beneath the skin’s surface, creating friction and complicating regrowth.

In contrast, a single- or double-blade razor trims hair cleanly at the surface, reducing skin damage and delivering a smoother, gentler shave. But I found the BIC Flex 5 Sensitive razor to be the best of both worlds. Covering the ground of a five-blade razor with the softness of a one-blade razor.

Not only did it speed up the admittedly long process of pubic shaving, but it did so without destroying my most delicate skin. The only trade-off here is that this razor doesn’t get quite as close as other, less-gentle blades. Still, it gets much closer than the trimmers on this list, and nearly as close as the Gillette Intimate Razor. Besides, going entirely bald down here is rarely a goal of mine, so I saw this as a positive.

If you’re looking to go as close to bald as possible, this is your best option. Designed specifically for body grooming, this razor features a compact, ultra-grippy handle that minimizes the risk of dropping and helps you maintain control while in the shower (or contorting yourself to reach every part of your groin). The blades are about as spaced out from each other as I’ve seen on any razor, which helps prevent clogging—something that is even more common when dealing with thick body hair.

Surrounding the two blades are a lubricating strip, an anti-ingrown bar, and an anti-irritation bar that work to reduce friction and help prevent trapped hairs. Plus, the blade head sits on a flexible pivoting disc, which helps the razor follow the contours of your body for smoother, more consistent contact with the skin.

Testing Notes: I’m not usually one to go completely bald below the waist, but this razor makes a strong case for it. It left my skin smooth and irritation-free without any lingering bumps in the days following, which is something I’ve found to be common when dealing with body razors. The grip is incredible and the pivoting head makes getting into the nooks and crannies of your body easy.

Before diving into the most intimate of manscaping, it’s important to consider a few key components of the device you’ll be using, given the sensitivity of the region. Not only to avoid any dreaded nicks or cuts, but also to ensure that the process is completed as seamlessly as possible.

Whenever you’re dealing with a trimmer of any kind, the battery life is one of the most prominent considerations. No one wants their device to sputter out and die when they’ve only managed to trim half their beard, and the same is true for the nether regions. Sure, it may be less noticeable than having half a beard, but it can still be uncomfortable. Look for devices that can hold a charge for at least an hour; this should guarantee you two to three sessions per charge.

Any less and you’re going to have to really be diligent with charging after every use or run the risk of it dying out before the next job’s done. The easiest way to avoid this scenario is to look for a rechargeable device, but more on that in a sec.

If you’re a committed pubic trimmer and never travel without one, look for the lighter options to ensure you can comfortably keep them in a carry-on or bag without weighing yourself down. While the TSA and airlines do not generally have a weight limit specifically for grooming devices, they do limit the weight of your bags, so we recommend sticking to trimmers that are under 10 oz to avoid too much bulk. Plus, if you’re new to this type of thing, steering away from tools that are heavier than this until you get a better idea of the process will help you avoid any painful slip-ups.

Similarly, how often do you change up your overall manscaping look? If you find yourself often changing up lengths and styles, you’re going to want to grab a device with multiple attachments and length options. The Braun Series 9 is the best-case scenario here, as it comes packed with nine attachments that create a total of 40 (!) length options. On the other hand, if you typically go full bald or keep it one consistent length, focus on the device’s head shape and blade material or close shaving ability rather than the number of attachments.

For the closest shave (outside of a cartridge razor), look to stainless steel or metal blades, as these can handle the most motor power and are more adept at plowing through thicker hair. While most of the trimmers on this list (and pubic trimmers in general) do not list their official motor power, having stainless steel blades is often the best indicator of a powerful tool, as it shows the brand looks towards the highest quality materials and performance available.

Not to mention, stainless steel blades are typically easier to clean. That being said, the risk of nicks and cuts is higher, so if you’re new to pubic trimming, opt for ceramic or plastic blades. These are gentler on skin, though they won’t get you as close to bare skin.

Use a rechargeable pubic trimmer to avoid mid-trim shutdowns and eliminate the need for spare batteries. Keep it charged between 30 percent and 80 percent to maintain performance and prevent it from dying when you need it most.

Do you prefer to do your manscaping in or outside of the shower? There is no wrong answer, but whichever you prefer is worth keeping in mind when choosing a trimmer. Some are made to be used wet, like the Philips Norelco OneBlade, while others not so much. If you’re a dedicated shower groomer, focus on the fully waterproof options.

As Men’s Health’s grooming editor, I test electric razors and similar devices for a living. When it comes to pubic trimmers, we’ve been testing these devices for nearly three years since this story was first published in 2023. For this update, I tested or retested over 15 pubic trimmers and razors, while consulting with skin and haircare experts on which tools they recommend in 2026.

I also considered top-reviewed trimmers that had high customer ratings on trusted e-commerce websites. After putting each device to the test, I evaluated its effectiveness, safety, and value. Following 12 months of testing, these seven tools proved to be the best for the job.

1. First and foremost, make sure you have ample time and are not rushed. This is not something you want to speed through.

2. Position yourself in front of a mirror with good lighting to make sure you have good visibility for all the crevices.

3. Grab your trimmer and pick your desired length. If you plan to fully shave your pubic hair, set the length long enough to shave easily but not too long—about a couple of days’ worth of stubble. If you’re trimming, start with a longer setting than you want at first; you can always trim it shorter later.

4. Apply baby powder on your pubic area while it’s dry to help soak up extra moisture and plump up the hair.

5. With short, gentle strokes, use the trimmer to cut the hair. Pubic hair grows in a variety of directions, so you’ll want to go slow and possibly go over the same areas a few times. For your scrotum and shaft, go extra slow and stretch the skin to flatten it and make it easier to trim. If you’re trimming your buttcheeks, crack, or perineum, you may want to place a hand mirror on the floor to help see where you’re trimming. You can also place one leg on a tub or toilet to make the area easier to see.

6. If you’re happy with the trim job, then you’re done! Hop in the shower to wash off.

7. If you’re going to shave completely, once you’re out of the shower, apply a pre-shave oil and shaving cream to the areas you’re going to shave. The key here is not to be stingy with the cream.

8. When you’re taking a razor to your nether regions, you’ll want to be extra careful. Shave with the grain of the hair in short, slow strokes. Do not—I repeat—do not rush. You’ll want to use the same stretching technique on your scrotum and shaft as you did while trimming, and the mirror is ideal if you’re taking the razor around back.

9. Make sure to rinse the razor frequently to avoid clogs and reapply shaving cream as needed.

10. Once you’re done, hop back in the shower to rinse everything away.

11. Apply a moisturizer or body oil to the area to help keep it protected. You may also want to apply a moisturizer or anti-chafe product regularly (like at least once a day) to help reduce friction, which can cause irritation on shaved skin, especially below the belt.

Maybe you’re a regular manscaper, or perhaps you just took the plunge into trimming out your nether regions. Regardless, one truth holds true: As soon as you take off the hair, it blooms right back again.

Sure, it might seem that your pubic hair is on a steroid-fueled regrowth. But that’s actually something of an optic illusion, says Dr. Alexes Hazen, MD, a reconstructive and cosmetic plastic surgeon at NYU Langone Health.

People who trim or shave their pubic hair often believe it grows faster than the hair on their head, but that’s a misconception, she says. We merely notice hair growth more and its speed when it’s shorter.

With pubic hair—and other body hair—the entire process takes about 30 to 44 days, Dr. Hazen says. That means the same pubes that started to grow will shed in about a month to a month and a half.

#5035. Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom: The AI Stock Winners and Losers After Jensen Huang’s Ousting

Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom: The AI Stock Winners and Losers After Jensen Huang’s Ousting

Wall Street is picking winners and losers from Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and the market is treating the chipmaker's competitors considerably better than companies tied to its business.

Nvidia shares fell 4.59% to $165.75 Thursday afternoon, recovering from an opening price of $151.01 and an intraday low of $148.80.

The rebound softened an initial collapse of more than 14%, but the stock remained firmly in negative territory.

The selloff followed Huang's immediate resignation as CEO, president, and board member after reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, although the company has not established that corporate secrets were compromised.

The stock was already in trouble before Huang stepped down. Nvidia had lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market capitalization between October 6 and November 6, raising questions about AI spending even before the leadership crisis intensified.

AMD climbed 5.79% to $584.89 after opening at $569.28, making it one of the clearest beneficiaries of Thursday's trading.

The company competes directly with Nvidia in AI accelerators, and uncertainty around Nvidia's leadership could make customers more interested in diversifying their chip suppliers.

Broadcom followed a similar trajectory, gaining 5.65% to $364.73 from an opening price of $356.80.

Unlike AMD, which competes through its own GPU products, Broadcom specializes in custom AI processors and networking technology, offering large customers a different way to reduce their dependence on Nvidia.

Google’s parent company Alphabet also advanced, rising 2.06% to $299.49 after opening at $293.77.

Those alternatives existed before Huang resigned, and Thursday's gains do not establish that Nvidia has lost customers. Investors may simply be pricing in better competitive opportunities if the leadership transition disrupts Nvidia's strategy or customer relationships.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave suffered a much rougher session, falling 7.49% to $56.22 after opening at $50.91.

Its decline came just one day after the cloud provider surged 24.7% following quarterly revenue growth of 168%, so this may be just as much a correction after an explosive movement as it is a reaction to Huang’s ousting.

In any case, the relationship between the companies helps explain the anxiety among investors. Nvidia invested another $2 billion in CoreWeave in January and has an initial $6.3 billion agreement to purchase unused computing capacity through April 2032, making it an investor, supplier, and customer of the same company.

Any change in Nvidia's investment priorities could therefore affect CoreWeave beyond ordinary chip purchases, although neither company has announced changes to those agreements.

The pressure also reached the semiconductor supply chain. TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's advanced processors, fell 1.15% to $408.61 after opening at $394.62, while memory supplier Micron lost 2.70%, trading at $789.43 after opening at $769.31.

SK Hynix, another major supplier of high-bandwidth memory used in AI hardware, declined 3% to $137.98 from an opening price of $134.25.

These companies depend on broader chip demand, however, so their losses cannot be attributed entirely to Nvidia's leadership problems.

For investors, the immediate concern is less about whether AI chips will stop selling and more about how Nvidia manages its partnerships, financing commitments, and product roadmap without the executive who built much of that network.

Nvidia's board has said it expects operations and customer commitments to continue without interruption. The company is scheduled to report quarterly earnings on November 17, with Kress now leading the business through its first earnings announcement since Huang's departure.

#5034. Hyperliquid leapfrogs Bybit, Kraken and OKX in open interest as Q3 positions grow 80%

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

Hyperliquid’s Q3 revenue rose 22% to $191 million as daily traders hit a record and stock-linked trading volumes surged.

Hyperliquid closed out the third quarter with a record $16.8 billion in open derivatives positions following a July slowdown.

Open interest jumped nearly 80% from the end of June, according to a new report from the Hyperliquid Research Collective. This was enough for Hyperliquid to surpass centralized exchange rivals Bybit, Kraken and OKX in open interest.

Its share of open interest across Hyperliquid and eight major exchanges climbed to 11.7%, up from 9.6% three months earlier.

This came alongside an uptick in crypto trading, with native perpetuals volume climbing from $109.5 billion in July to more than $188 billion in September. Average daily traders also hit a quarterly record of 65,161.

Protocol revenue rose 21.7% quarter over quarter to nearly $191 million, including $17.3 million earned from its USDC reserve-income arrangement tied to Coinbase's role as Hyperliquid's treasury deployer. Revenue remained 36.5% below the same period last year.

Stock-linked perpetuals volume also rose 161% to $153.8 billion, overtaking the commodities asset class in HIP-3, which lets third-party operators launch perp futures.

Wintermute, one of crypto's biggest market makers, has become a major user of Hyperliquid's auctions for early access to trading data, Bloomberg reported Thursday.

A wallet linked to Wintermute won 76% of auctions for the top-priority data slot over the preceding month, according to analysis from Loris Tools and cited by Bloomberg.

The system gives traders an early look at incoming orders, allowing them to change their positions before other orders are processed. Critics say the feature gives larger firms an unfair advantage. Wintermute defended it as a transparent way to compete for speed.

#5032. The 10 Best Red Light Therapy Tools of 2026, Tested by Beauty Experts

Our top picks—from Omnilux, TheraFace, and Qure—treat acne, boost collagen, and more.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

If you're starting to notice that your skin is looking a little, well, tired, you're not alone. The visible signs of aging—I’m talking fine lines and wrinkles, dullness, even sallow skin—will strike us all sooner or later. Bummer. On the bright side, we're living in an age when there's no shortage of smart beauty devices and skincare products for these issues. From wrinkle-smoothing injections like Botox and fillers to anti-aging creams, you've got an arsenal of skin-boosting tools at your disposal.

But what if I were to tell you that there's one such solution that takes roughly 10 a day and can be done while you're relaxing in bed scrolling TikTok? Enter red light therapy.

Red light therapy has exploded in popularity lately because it's convenient, noninvasive, and can be done at home. It uses a specific spectrum of visible light that offers a host of beauty benefits—low-level laser light therapy can effectively treat scars, vitiligo, and psoriasis, research shows. It has an anti-inflammatory effect and can even help to smooth wrinkles, too. So, how does it work? We know that red light penetrates 2 to 3 millimeters into skin's dermis, where it's “absorbed by light-sensitive porphyrins in the mitochondria of skin cells, stimulating energy production in fibroblasts to churn out more collagen,” says dermatologist Ava Shamban, MD.

But the goodness doesn't stop there. Red light can also help fade dark spots and manage eczema, plus boost hair growth, says dermatologist Purvisha Patel, MD. These at-home devices can be expensive, but they're an investment you can use for a years to come: Many red light therapy tools are also equipped with blue lights, which are particularly effective at treating acne (say buh-bye to those period or menopausal breakouts) and other concerns. Bottom line: At any age—and for years to come—these red light therapy tools can be a beneficial addition to your beauty routine.

Ultimately, these are the devices that we’ll continue to use and would genuinely repurchase if we had to start our skincare routine from scratch. The best part? Our faves start at just $72, which is a major win for a category that easily ranges from $300 to $700.

I've got a great list of options for you, but if you find yourself in the market for a red light therapy tool, here are a few things to keep in mind.

There are several kinds of red light therapy devices to choose from, including panels, masks, and facial wands, and one may be a better fit for you based on your lifestyle and the area you're seeking to treat.

LED masks are the most common variety you'll find for home use because most are hands-free and contain a lot of diodes (a fancy way of referring to the individual lightbulbs), offering a powerful burst of light to treat the face, neck, or chest.

Maybe you're claustrophobic and the idea of wearing masks gives you the heebie-jeebies—that's where panels come in. They look like flexible bodyboards that you lie down under, and they come in a diverse range of shapes and sizes, each offering different levels of red light exposure to your face, décolletage, and back. These also help replace the need for a separate lip-specific red light therapy tool.

Wands are appealing when you want to target smaller specific areas (the crow's feet or smile lines, for example) and prefer to do your treatments on the go (you can walk around while using these).

Our eyes are the first place to show signs of aging, so you’ll want to take a cue from dermatologist Pooja Rambhia, MD, and use these affordable red light therapy eye tools. Red, deep red, and near-infrared wavelengths target fine lines, wrinkles, darkness, and puffiness early on, making them a smart preventive beauty move.

It's tempting to pick a device with the quickest treatment window, especially if you don't have loads of free time to sit back and chill with a red light mask. But remember: To treat more advanced signs of aging, a longer treatment time may be more beneficial. Look at the full picture before you base your purchase on the convenience of a quicker treatment. And for what it’s worth, almost all of our featured recommendations can be used in just three minutes, so even busy women can incorporate quick treatments into their routine.

You may notice the abbreviation nm on the outer packaging of many of these tools. This stands for nanometers and refers to the wavelength of the light that the device emits—an important metric to consider, says dermatologist Jody A. Levine, MD. "Red light typically falls between 630 and 660 nanometers, and is good for targeting fine lines and mild discoloration," says Dr. Levine. If you're looking for something slightly more powerful—to deal with deeper wrinkles, sagging, or stubborn pigmentary problems—go with a device that cranks up to the near-infrared range (between 800 and 850 nanometers) to penetrate deeper.

Our beauty team is well-versed in red light therapy tools. We’ve been updating this story since December 2022—and I’ve been writing about these devices since November 2019. I've also been using red light therapy tools since April 2018. They've significantly diminished my stubborn fine lines and hyperpigmentation—and when I stop for a few months, they slowly reappear. Consistency is key, so we tested dozens of red light therapy devices for over two years to determine which ones are worth purchasing and can help us maintain wrinkle-free skin.

Since there are quite literally thousands of options available on Amazon alone, I asked dermatologists about their no-fail picks. Next, I recruited WH staffers—beauty director Brian Underwood, associate style & commerce editor Shannen Zitz, and associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian—and our beauty contributors—Erica Metzger, Lily Wohlner, and Lisa DeSantis—for their suggestions. After compiling a comprehensive list of promising new launches, old standbys, and products that align with derm guidance, we got to testing.

We spent a minimum of three weeks evaluating attributes like ease of use, treatment time, comfort, any tangible results, and overall value. Of the 22 devices tested, these 10 delivered the best results in our in-depth testing process.

Beyond keeping expert guidance in mind—type, nanometers, and time commitment—we considered our long- and short-term results. CurrentBody Skin has quickly become my go-to brand for smart beauty devices. I’ve recently featured the line in our guide to the best red light therapy eye masks. Qure's various LED lights are within the correct wavelength range to treat multiple skin concerns. For example, acne-fighting blue light should be between 400 and 500nm (Qure's is 415nm), while near-infrared is most helpful between 760 and 1,400nm.

I've got a great list of options for you, but if you find yourself in the market for a red light therapy tool, here are a few things to keep in mind.

There are several kinds of red light therapy devices to choose from, including panels, masks, and facial wands, and one may be a better fit for you based on your lifestyle and the area you're seeking to treat.

LED masks are the most common variety you'll find for home use because most are hands-free and contain a lot of diodes (a fancy way of referring to the individual light sources), offering a burst of light to treat the face, neck, or chest.

Maybe you're claustrophobic and the idea of wearing masks gives you the heebie-jeebies—that's where panels come in. They look like flexible bodyboards that you lie down under, and they come in a diverse range of shapes and sizes, each offering different levels of red light exposure to your face, décolletage, and back. These also help replace the need for a separate lip-specific red light therapy tool.

Wands are appealing when you want to target smaller specific areas (the crow's feet or smile lines, for example) and like to do your treatments on the go (you can walk around while using these).

Our eyes are the first place to show signs of aging, so you’ll want to take a cue from dermatologist Pooja Rambhia, MD, and use these affordable red light therapy eye tools. They target fine lines, wrinkles, darkness, and puffiness early on, making them a smart preventive beauty move.

It's tempting to pick a device with the quickest treatment window, especially if you don't have loads of free time to sit back and chill with a red light mask. But remember: To treat more advanced signs of aging, a longer treatment time may be more beneficial. Look at the full picture before you base your purchase on the convenience of a quicker treatment. And for what it’s worth, almost all of our featured recommendations can be used in just three minutes, so even busy women can incorporate quick treatments into their routine.

You may notice the abbreviation nm on the outer packaging of many of these tools. This stands for nanometers and refers to the wavelength of the light that the device emits—an important metric to consider, says dermatologist Jody A. Levine, MD. "Red light typically falls between 630 and 660 nanometers, and is good for targeting fine lines and mild discoloration," says Dr. Levine. If you're looking for something slightly more powerful—to deal with deeper wrinkles, sagging, or stubborn pigmentary problems—go with a device that cranks up to the near-infrared range (between 800 and 850 nanometers) to penetrate deeper.

Our beauty team is well-versed in red light therapy tools. We’ve been updating this story since December 2022—and I’ve been writing about these devices since November 2019. I've also been using red light therapy tools since April 2018. They've significantly diminished my stubborn fine lines and hyperpigmentation—and when I stop for a few months, they slowly reappear. Consistency is key, so we tested dozens of red light therapy devices for over two years to determine which ones are worth purchasing and can help us maintain wrinkle-free skin.

Since there are quite literally thousands of options available on Amazon alone, I asked dermatologists about their no-fail picks. Next, I recruited WH staffers—beauty director Brian Underwood, associate style & commerce editor Shannen Zitz, and associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian—and our beauty contributors—Erica Metzger, Lily Wohlner, and Lisa DeSantis—for their suggestions. After compiling a comprehensive list of promising new launches, old standbys, and products that align with derm guidance, we got to testing.

We spent a minimum of three weeks evaluating attributes like ease of use, treatment time, comfort, any tangible results, and overall value. Of the 22 devices tested, these 10 delivered the best results in our in-depth testing process.

Beyond keeping expert guidance in mind—type, nanometers, and time commitment—we considered our long- and short-term results. We also considered each product’s durability over the years, and eliminated anything that doesn’t remain in top shape. Ahem, don’t forget to clean your LED face masks to help with their longevity. We also tried the latest drops and the Women’s Health Beauty Award-winning Solawave Neck & Chest Pro Light Therapy Mask took the crown as our favorite launch of the year. Ultimately, these are the devices that we’ll continue to use and would genuinely repurchase if we had to start our skincare routine from scratch. The best part? Our faves start at just $72, which is a major win for a category that easily ranges from $300 to $700.

In-office LED lights operate at more powerful strengths than at-home devices, which increases efficacy. So, with professional treatments, you may see better results in less time, but that doesn't mean you should dismiss the at-home devices altogether. They're still helpful for treating common skin conditions like the odd breakout or fine lines, but it could take up to six months to start seeing results, says Dr. Sperling. Our experts also say they're a great way to maintain the results from any in-office treatments you may be receiving.

If you want to get faster and more effective results at home without a trip to your dermatologist's office or a medi-spa, Dr. Patel recommends using your device more often—if possible daily.

While many red light devices are generally safe, start out by using yours once or twice a week to make sure your skin doesn't have any reactions. Once you've confirmed that your skin can tolerate it, Dr. Sperling says you can increase the frequency, according to the brand’s instructions.You can use your red light therapy device in the morning or at night, but ideally, it should be done on clean, dry, product-free skin after you cleanse your face. However, Dr. Patel notes that if you use a red light therapy tool after a serum, it'll help the product penetrate more deeply into the skin—just patch test on some skin before you do it on the whole face.

It sounds obvious, but read the instructions carefully and don’t use the device on infected skin, says Dr. Patel. Most LED face masks come with goggles to shield your eyes; wearing them offers essential protection. And, be sure that you don't fall asleep with the mask or tool on your face longer than instructed or it can result in scars and burns, says Dr. Camp. Most tools have an auto turn-off feature, but if yours doesn’t, then set a timer on your smartphone.

Tommy John earned the crown for the best overall pajamas due to their übersoft second-skin fabric, so it's no shock that the brand's underwear exceeds our expectations, too. What sets these apart from others is the micro modal and spandex blend, which feels unreal—like ridiculously smooth against the skin. We're talking a fabric so luxurious that it makes regular cotton feel rough in comparison. Based on our testing, this pair of trunks nails the perfect balance of stretch and structure with their four-way stretch, so they move with you no matter how active (or lazy) your day gets.

Unlike other trunks that call for constant tugging or readjusting, these stayed perfectly in place, whether we were sitting, standing, or running errands around town. The quick-draw fly makes using the bathroom easier and faster in the middle of the night. On humid days, these are a lifesaver. Despite us breaking a sweat, this underwear stayed fresh, which speaks to their exceptional level of odor resistance. And even after multiple washes, the softness doesn't diminish—a true sign of premium quality.

Sunspel’s Classic Boxer Shorts are hands down some of the best out there, and once you try them, you’ll get it. This pair is made by a U.K. brand with over a century of experience perfecting the essentials, so it's time-tested. These boxers are cut from long-staple cotton, meaning the fibers are longer, the fabric is softer, and it'll last for the long haul. Basically, it feels ridiculously comfortable—like you’re lounging in luxury every time you put it on—and it stays that way wear after wear.

One standout feature is the distinctive back panel. Sunspel uses a single smooth panel across the rear versus an uncomfortable central seam running down the middle. For us, that meant no chafing, no awkward pressure, and no irritation, even when we were sitting at our work desk or running quick errands. The fabric is lightweight but strong, so it breathes well and never bunches under pants. During testing, it held up all day, no matter what: long commutes, walking tours on vacation, or casual bike rides. We don't recommend wearing this pair under gym shorts, but you can reserve it for days of less sweat-inducing activity since it's all cotton.

They’ve got this easy, relaxed fit that gives you full range of motion, but the tailoring keeps them from feeling baggy or sloppy. And then there’s the design: They’re finished with a super gentle waistband that sits comfortably. We also love that there's solid colors as well as striped patterns. It's the kind that makes you rethink the whole category. They’re built for comfort but stylish enough to feel special, which is exactly what you want from a pair you’ll wear day in and day out.

I normally wouldn’t trust underwear that costs under $10 to compete with premium pairs, but Uniqlo’s trunks are the exception. The Japanese retailer offers some of the best basics around, delivering impressive quality at an affordable price, including these boxer shorts, which are especially comfortable in the heat. They’re made with a breathable woven cotton fabric, which feels much lighter than any knit underwear I own. When the temps went up to 100 degrees in New York last week, these kept me cool all day.

The fit is more open and roomy than my briefs, so my crown jewels had plenty of breathing room and even caught a breeze when I was lounging around. I also love how they lie flat under shorts and linen pants, though I would skip wearing slim trousers since the fabric can bunch. Even though the waistband is scrunched, it sits gently against my skin without causing any irritation. When my Sunspel pair is in the laundry, I’ll even wear it to bed on warm nights. For such an inexpensive style, it holds up over time. I’ve washed it multiple times without seeing a single loose seam or noticing any shrinkage. Plus, the striped pattern looks timeless, so it doesn’t feel like a bargain-bin underwear.

I can always count on mesh fabric to keep me cool when I need it most, which is why I love this underwear. SAXX uses a polyester-elastane mesh with an open, dotted texture that lets heat and moisture escape, so I never feel clammy. Even when I sweat, the fabric never gets waterlogged and dries incredibly fast. It’s one of my go-to pairs for workouts, especially on heavy cardio days. The hammock-style pouch keeps everything secure and supported while I’m biking or running on the treadmill, and the fit is snugger than most boxer shorts, specifically around the butt, thigh, and legs.

The 6-inch inseam stops mid-thigh, while the high waist sits right under your belly button. I can wear them under just about any pair of pants without worrying about bunching or visible lines. The compression-like fit may feel too snug if you prefer a roomier boxer short. And the mesh fabric isn’t as soft or natural-feeling as cotton or modal, so it may not be everyone’s favorite pair for lounging all day. The good thing is the pack of three can get you through half the week, especially if you stock up.

If you’re ready to upgrade from basic cotton underwear, CDLP is where I’d start. I love the Tencel Lyocell fabric that has an incredibly silky, almost cooling feel against my skin. It’s surprisingly breathable, too, so I never feel overheated on days when the temps spike to 90 degrees. It strikes a nice balance between feeling luxurious and being practical. The snug fit hugs my body without squeezing too tightly. It rests just below the waist and has a 3.8-inch inseam that sits high on the upper thigh and hides under my short shorts. Some of the more expensive pairs tend to pill, but the fabric on this one keeps its smooth, premium feel even after multiple washes. The only real drawback is the price, but if you’re willing to splurge on a single pair of underwear, the comfort makes it feel well worth it.

Quality underwear doesn't have to cost a fortune. Take Uniqlo's Airism Ultra Seamless Boxer Briefs, which clock in under $20 and also fit like a glove. During my testing, the cutoff waist felt invisible, sitting flush against the skin without squeezing or rolling, like it was made just for me. Despite its close-hugging cut, there's a fair amount of stretch to accommodate you running up the stairs, twisting in your chair, or walking briskly through crowded city streets.

Overall, I found this pair to be lightweight, super breathable, and packed with new moisture-wicking technology that helps to keep you fresh, cool, and dry around the clock. Whether it's a hot day or you're working up a sweat at the gym, Airism pulls moisture away from your skin, making sure you don't feel swampy down under.

Every Sunday at my house is wash day, but this underwear has survived through every last cycle without losing its allure. Our only gripe is that Uniqlo Airism sells out very fast, which means you have to wait for the occasional restock—so get them now.

Cotton is the OG of underwear fabrics, and our testers found that it's the most comfortable knit for everyday fits. Take note: while cotton is pretty breathable, it doesn't do a great job of wicking away moisture. That's why our fashion editors do not recommend cotton skivvies for working out. In some cases, a pair of undies that's 100% cotton tends to lose shape over time and can give a swamp-ass feeling. If you have money to spend, we recommend trying a long-staple or organic cotton, which is more premium and durable.

Nylon is moisture-wicking and super durable, so the fabric won’t pill or stretch out. However, a little spandex (aka elastane) in the fabric helps for movement and extra comfort. Plus, it dries quickly too, so you won't feel sticky post-workout.

Imagine cotton, but smoother and a little fancier. Modal has a silky-soft feel that's light and cool against your skin. Testers say their favorite modal boxer briefs almost disappear under their clothes.

If you're looking to keep your precious cargo secure, then briefs provide the most security. However, if you want to let the package breathe, then boxers are your best bet. Remember: Boxers tend to ride up when you're wearing slim pants, which is why we recommend only wearing them with more relaxed fits.

If you need extra support, we recommend underwear with a pouch or a snugger fit around the waistband. For some men with testicular pain or discomfort, they may want to find a style that fits well and doesn't ride up or bunch, as this could aggravate their symptoms.

Your underwear is the first thing you put on and the last thing you take off, so it has to work with you, not against you, all day long. If it doesn't do its job, you'll feel it, whether it's discomfort, chafing, or overheating.

Think about it: excellent underwear isn't just about looking cool (though that's like icing on the cake). It's about how it performs in real life. Are you lounging at home? Going for a long run? Stuck on a flight for hours? Each of these scenarios demands something different. You need underwear that supports your lifestyle, whether that's stretch for flexibility, moisture-wicking for sweat, or breathability to keep things fresh down yonder.

The best breathable underwear manages heat and moisture so sweat can escape instead of getting trapped against your skin. Many use micro-knit or mesh-like weaves that create tiny air channels within the fabric, allowing heat to dissipate and air to circulate as you move. Others incorporate moisture-wicking fibers to pull sweat away from the body and spread it across the surface of the fabric so it evaporates faster. Some brands even add targeted “cool zones” or thinner panels in high-sweat areas to boost airflow where you need it most.

When underwear can’t breathe, moisture builds up, leading to overheating, chafing, irritation, and odor. Breathable underwear works with your body by keeping things cooler, drier, and more comfortable throughout the day. For Men’s Health guys, breathability makes a difference for everyday wear, long commutes, desk jobs, workouts, travel days, and humid conditions. It’s especially clutch for guys who sweat easily, live in hot climates, train hard, or spend long stretches in the same pair from morning to night.

As part of the Men’s Health style team, led by our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, I’ve tested some of the best—and worst—underwear on the market firsthand. Since 2015, our team has worn, washed, and stressed-tested more than 100 pairs across every major style, brand, and fabric imaginable, from classic cotton briefs to high-tech performance boxer briefs and luxe everyday upgrades.

Testing wasn't limited to just one body type or fit preference. In addition to my own wear tests, multiple Men's Health editors with different builds pitched in, spanning sizes from small through XXL. This allowed us to see how each pair fit and performed across a wide range of body types, rises, thigh sizes, and proportions—and to flag issues like inconsistent sizing, rolling waistbands, or fabric that only works on one kind of frame.

I wore each pair repeatedly in real-life situations, including workdays, workouts, commutes, travel, and weekend outings. I looked at how each pair performed over time, paying close attention to whether fabrics remained soft without pilling, waistbands held their shape, seams avoided chafing, and support held up after hours of movement. I judged each pair on fabric quality, fit, breathability, odor control, stretch and recovery, durability after repeated washes, and comfort levels ranging from morning to night. Only the pairs that consistently delivered comfort, support, and long-term performance earned a spot on this list. What you’ll find here are the top 12 best men’s underwear options that rose to the top after years of hands-on testing by the Men’s Health team.

Boxers: They’re classic, loose-fitting shorts that are lightweight, with lots of breathing room, and zero restriction. They’re great for lounging or sleeping because they feel airy and relaxed, but that same looseness makes them less practical under slim pants. Fabric can bunch, ride up, and offer little to no support if you’re moving around a lot. Boxer briefs: They’re cut like boxers but fit snugly like briefs. That means they hug your thighs, hold everything in place, and layer smoothly under jeans, trousers, or even gym shorts. They also prevent chafing since the fabric creates a barrier between your thighs—a lifesaver if you walk a lot or hit the gym. The tradeoff? They’re less airy than boxers, but most guys prefer the balance of comfort, coverage, and support.

That really depends on your laundry schedule. If you’re someone who does laundry once a week, aim for at least 10 to 12 pairs so you’ve got a little cushion. If laundry happens less often—say every two weeks—you’ll probably want 15 to 20 pairs. If you’re very active, then consider stocking your drawer with 25 to 30 pairs. Basically, you want enough to last until wash day plus a couple extra for workouts, surprise trips, or the occasional lazy Sunday when you just don’t feel like doing laundry.

A good rule of thumb: it’s reasonable to refresh your stash every six to 12 months, but quality underwear can last longer depending on fabric, frequency of wear, washing, and condition. If the elastic’s shot, they’re sagging, developing holes, or the fabric’s thinning, that’s your cue to toss them. Think of it as a rotation—you don’t need to replace everything at once, but gradually swap in new pairs so you’re always stocked with comfortable, supportive ones.

Every man has worn them at some point; boxers are light and loose and so freeing. They're the classic underwear style for men that feels very relaxed with short legs. This type of underwear is perfect for lounging around the house, sleeping, or wearing under relaxed-fit pants. Also comes in a variety of prints and patterns (hello, personality).

Think speedo. Think upside-down triangle. Briefs provide the required coverage and optimal support while exposing more skin for ease of mobility. Here, there's no risk of leg fabric riding up (because there's none).

Perhaps the most popular one, it's a hybrid of loose-fit boxers and tight briefs, offering a solid balance of support and comfort. If you’re not a fan of underwear that rides up too high, go for boxer briefs that have a longer leg and a snug fit, like compression underwear that’s perfect for the gym. They should skim the leg versus squeezing you too tight.

Like the title says, a trunk is similar to boxer briefs but with a shorter cut—halfway up the thigh. It's best for guys who want something fitted but less fabric around the leg. For some visual assistance, think of trunks as the underwear style that most CK models wear on big billboards.

It depends on personal preference, comfort, and the activity. Here's a quick breakdown to help guide your choice, weighing the pros and cons of both.

Tight underwear (e.g., briefs, boxer briefs) provides better support, which is especially useful for physical activities like running or working out. This type reduces chafing and prevents excessive movement, which can help with comfort throughout the day. Works well under slim-fit pants, as it avoids bunching and creates a cleaner silhouette. If it's too tight, it can restrict airflow and potentially cause discomfort or sweating, especially in warmer weather. Overly tight fits might not be ideal for guys concerned about reproductive health, though the effect is typically negligible with properly sized underwear.

On the other hand, loose underwear is better suited for lounging or casual, low-impact activities since it allows more airflow and freedom of movement. It feels more breathable, making it ideal for hotter climates or relaxed settings. Also, loose underwear can be paired with loose-fit pants for added comfort. This option lacks support, which feel uncomfortable during workouts or physical activity. Plus, it can cramp your style—bunching up under tighter pants and offering a restrictive feel.

If you want to protect the structural integrity of your underwear's waistband, the best way to keep them from stretching is to hand wash them and hang them dry. But given how impractical that is, the second best option is to put them in the washing machine on cold water and use a low dryer setting so the elastic doesn't warp. However, our testers say that most of the pairs they've tried have kept their waistbands' shapes even after several trips to the laundromat. If your underwear's waistband has lost its shape, you're probably overdue to replace it.

Even the best underwear won’t last if you don’t take care of it properly. Washing underwear inside out helps remove sweat and bacteria more effectively while protecting the fabric’s surface. Cold or warm water is usually best, as hot water can break down elastic fibers and cause shrinkage over time. Skip harsh detergents and fabric softeners, especially for performance or moisture-wicking underwear. Softeners can coat fibers and reduce breathability and odor control. When possible, air-drying is ideal, as high heat from dryers is the fastest way to kill stretch and warp waistbands. If you do use a dryer, stick to low heat.

#5029. Who Is Colette Kress, Jensen Huang’s Successor as Nvidia CEO?

Who Is Colette Kress, Jensen Huang’s Successor as Nvidia CEO?

For the first time in 33 years, someone other than Jensen Huang is running Nvidia. And the person taking over is not an engineer, a chip designer, or a Silicon Valley founder.

Colette Kress, Nvidia's 59-year-old chief financial officer, was named interim CEO Thursday following Huang's abrupt resignation amid reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.

Kress will remain CFO while the board searches for a permanent replacement, according to Nvidia's regulatory filing. She inherits a company worth trillions of dollars, a shaken investor base, and a management structure built around one man.

Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013, when it was primarily known for graphics cards used in video games. She arrived with nearly 25 years of financial experience across some of America's largest technology companies.

She spent eight years at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. During her 13-year tenure there, she became CFO of the Server and Tools division, overseeing financial strategy for Microsoft's enterprise computing business.

In 2010, she moved to Cisco as senior vice president and CFO of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization, managing financial planning and business development across the networking giant's operations.

Kress holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University, according to her official biography.

Her move to Nvidia came with an unusual endorsement. Her two sons, then enthusiastic gamers, encouraged her to join the company responsible for the graphics chips powering their favorite games, according to Forbes.

Huang personally recruited her, explaining his vision for AI computing on a whiteboard during their discussions, Wired reported. At the time, Nvidia was the smallest company Kress had worked for.

When Kress joined Nvidia, its annual revenue stood at approximately $4.13 billion. By fiscal 2026, that figure had reached $215.9 billion, an increase of more than 50 times.

Huang drove Nvidia's technological strategy, but Kress oversaw the finances supporting its expansion from gaming hardware into data centers and AI infrastructure.

Her tenure included Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of networking specialist Mellanox and an increasingly aggressive strategy of investing in companies that purchase its computing hardware.

Those relationships now include CoreWeave, in which Nvidia invested another $2 billion in January. CoreWeave's rapid growth reflects enormous demand for Nvidia-powered computing, alongside the financial costs of building that infrastructure.

Kress also became Nvidia's principal financial voice to Wall Street, regularly explaining margins, chip demand and revenue forecasts during earnings calls.

Forbes ranked her among America's richest self-made women in 2026, with almost $750 million in Nvidia shares as of Wednesday's close.

Kress takes charge as Nvidia faces questions about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had already lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market value from its October peak before the board publicly announced its investigation on Huang’s love affairs.

She must also navigate Washington's restrictions on advanced chip exports to China and scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's commercial relationships. The board has said it has no reason to believe company secrets or U.S. national security were compromised in the allegations involving Huang.

Her financial expertise cannot entirely replace Huang's technical background or his personal relationships with developers, customers, and governments. Maintaining Nvidia's engineering leadership will require close coordination with the executives responsible for its chips and software.

Kress has promised to build on Huang's legacy, saying that “Nvidia's strength has always come from its people.”

Her first major public test arrives Tuesday, November 17, when Nvidia reports its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings. The company has scheduled its results for approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific, followed by an investor call at 2 p.m.

#5028. CFTC’s Selig accuses states of trying to ‘lock up’ prediction market founders

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

Chair Michael Selig defends federal oversight of prediction markets as states pursue enforcement and the CFTC presses its authority in court.

Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chair Michael Selig is turning up the heat on his criticisms of states' handling of lawsuits brought against prediction market platforms and their executives.

Speaking at the Cantor Convergence conference, Selig called the state suits "really egregious" and defended the platforms operating under what he has long called the CFTC's "exclusive jurisdiction."

"We're seeing states bring criminal charges, essentially trying to lock up founders and CEOs of these companies that are offering lawful products under a federal regime," he said.

The comments come amid a stretch of battles between the CFTC and roughly a dozen states and cities over whether event contracts offered on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket constitute illegal gambling. Selig argued that the disagreements should be hashed out in court without threatening executives with time in prison.

"Somebody says it's gambling, somebody says it's a derivative," he said. "That's not something that should be at the risk of going to jail."

And instead of fighting on a case-by-case basis in multiple states, Selig wants to see the issue raised to the Supreme Court in a bid to solidify the CFTC's authority.

"I don't understand whether we're going to have every major CEO of an exchange locked up in a jail cell in Utah, or if we can just go to the Supreme Court and hash this thing out on the merits," he said.

On Thursday, the Justice Department and CFTC sued Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin to block his action against Kalshi.

Louisiana also filed a lawsuit Thursday targeting companies including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase.

"I am concerned that some of the states are getting very aggressive," Selig said. "We’ll continue to defend our jurisdiction."
